recentItems.title: Eugene Fraser - an audio tribute
recentItems.description: An audio tribute to broadcaster Eugene Fraser whose death was announced in August 2026. His broadcasting career began in New Zealand in the early 1960s. He moved to the UK in the late 60s working for the BBC as a newsreader and presenter on Radios 1 and 2. In 1975 he joined Radio Victory in Portsmouth. Between 1977 and 1993 he was a newsreader and continuity announcer on BBC Radio 4.

recentItems.title: PM report on the closure of BBC Radio 4 long wave

recentItems.title: Closure of BBC Radio 4 long wave - BBC H&W feature
recentItems.description:
On Friday 26 June 2026 Malcolm Boyden, on the BBC Hereford & Worcester breakfast show, talked about the closure of BBC radio 4 long wave (from the 27th) which was transmitted from the Wychbold Masts near Droitwich (plus two replay sites in Scotland) in Worcestershire.
There's a report by Lindsay Alder who interviews Alastair Moseley from the Bromsgrove Society. Then Malcolm speaks to Nick Todderhill of the Radio Society of Great Britain.

recentItems.title: The Fifth Beaulieu Jazz Festival 1960 (audio only)
recentItems.description:
BBC television coverage (audio only) of the Fifth Beaulieu Jazz Festival held in the grounds of Palace House in Hampshire. Programme was scheduled for Saturday 30 July 1960 22.45-23.25 but taken off-air six minutes ahead of time when a riot broke out. Commentary by Derek Jones. Music from Acker Bilk and the Paramount Jazz Band. 

Recording was part of the stash of tapes taken to New Zealand by someone who emigrated there. His son, Mike Bailey, passed the tape onto Duncan Lockhart who kindly donated this audio to me.
